summaryEn: Teaches you to put a complement first for emphasis while the verb keeps its place.
Teaches you to speak memorably with a threefold list and a pause.
Teaches you to make an abstract idea concrete with an image.
Teaches you to meet hard questions and heckling calmly.
Teaches you to buy time and to give your talk a shape when you speak unprepared.
Teaches you to open an event, to build the links between its parts and to close it.
Teaches you to meet a barbed remark calmly and with grace.
Teaches you to tell an event along an arc of tension.
Teaches you to build a short farewell speech out of images and appreciation.
Teaches you to concede a point and still defend your case, with concessive conjunctions.
Teaches you idioms built on the body and the trap of translating them word for word.
Teaches you what idioms built on food really mean.
Teaches you idioms built on animals and the phrases that express trust.
Teaches you the metaphors of mood and atmosphere built on images of weather.
Teaches you idioms built on colours and the traps they carry.
Teaches you to express persistence and rivalry with idioms that come from sport.
Teaches you idioms about money and the phrases that express certainty.
Teaches you to describe power and influence with idioms that come from music.
Teaches you the trap of translating an idiom word for word, and how to look for the real equivalent.
Teaches you to use idioms in the right dose and in context.
Teaches you every form of the reporting mood and what it is for.
Teaches you to attribute a source and to report it in the language of a news agency.
Teaches you to report a finding in impersonal academic language.
Teaches you to separate a reported claim from a proven fact.
Teaches you to write the abstract of a study with academic patterns.
Teaches you to accept an objection and still defend your thesis, in academic language.
Teaches you to follow the expert language compressed into extended attributes.
Teaches you to simplify a complex subject without breaking what is true.
Teaches you to report a quotation faithfully and where distortion begins.
Teaches you to take the floor on a panel, to draw distinctions and to keep to time.
Teaches you to unpack the nominal language of contract clauses.
Teaches you the impersonal modal passive of standard terms and conditions.
Teaches you to build a claim with the function verb phrases of legal language.
Teaches you to relay a legal opinion in the reporting mood.
Teaches you the genitive-heavy language of data protection texts.
Teaches you to give a witness statement truthfully and to mark its limits.
Teaches you to defend a contested claim with concessive conjunctions.
Teaches you to discuss in legal language what taking on a guarantee means.
Teaches you to lodge an appeal that protects the deadline and to submit the grounds later.
Teaches you to follow courtroom language and the reporting of the record.
Teaches you to fold a relative clause in front of the noun and to unfold it again.
Teaches you to build the sense of what has to be done, with zu plus the participle.
Teaches you to find the core of a long sentence and to break it into parts.
Teaches you to move both ways between the nominal style and the verbal style.
Teaches you to build an aside in the right case and between commas.
Teaches you to bind a text together with the references inside it.
Teaches you to write short and clear by dropping what is not needed.
Teaches you to build a deliberate double meaning and to notice one.
Teaches you to turn the same content into different text types and registers.
Teaches you to tell apart the meanings of words that lie close together.
